C-TELEGRAM-BRIDGE-PLUGIN.Summary: Add a TelegramBridgePlugin server plugin that runs an in-process grammy long-polling Telegram bot inside the OpenCode server process, bridges private-chat DM forum topics to OpenCode sessions through the plugin context, uses a fixed General control topic plus one topic per active session whose title carries a live status emoji, keeps durable plugin-scoped state in ctx.storage including a message mirror map and durable final delivery, and adds model switching, interactive questions, manual permission buttons, subagent activity, message revert and fork, and file attachments, configured through an optional top-level telegram section in canonical vvoc schema v3.
C-TELEGRAM-BRIDGE-PLUGIN.Problem: Users want to drive several OpenCode sessions in parallel from a phone. OpenCode 2 runs one background server whose sessions are addressable by every client, and Telegram supports forum topics inside private chats, so a single DM bot can present one topic per session and steer them concurrently. Existing OpenCode Telegram bots are separate processes: the mature upstream bot is deliberately single-context, and the topic-based forks are group-first or couple to OpenCode's internal SQLite event log or a multiplexer identity. No existing solution is a vvoc-native server plugin that runs inside the OpenCode process, addresses OpenCode sessions directly, and presents private-DM topics with durable state, so this capability cannot be obtained by configuration or by wrapping an existing tool.

Goals.Goal: Register a single TelegramBridgePlugin as the twelfth vvoc server plugin, export it from the package root and a ./plugins/telegram subpath, and set it up in the aggregate VvocPlugin with reverse-order teardown that aborts the polling loop and releases every acquired runtime.

Run an in-process grammy long-polling gateway started in setup and stopped by the returned cleanup, guarded so exactly one gateway runs per OpenCode server process even when the plugin is set up for multiple locations, keyed on native app object identity.

Map one Telegram DM forum topic to one OpenCode session id, keep a fixed General topic as the command control lane, create a topic when a session becomes active, and close (never delete) a topic when the session stops being active after the configured recency window.

Expose control commands in the General topic — /new with a project picker, a single idempotent /sync that reconciles the displayed topic set to the active session set, /status with per-session context usage, and /help — and treat a plain text message in a session topic as a prompt to that session with streamed assistant output and abort support.

Render live session status as a leading emoji in the topic title (running, idle, waiting for a question, waiting for a permission, error, aborted) using throttled topic-title edits, with the clean session title preserved after the emoji.

Provide model switching from a session topic through /model as an inline picker over connected providers and their models with the current model marked; sessions are created with their project default agent and no agent switching surface exists.

Deliver interaction as manual inline-button permission approvals through ctx.permission and inline-button answers to agent questions with an explicit custom-answer flow, with no Guardian auto-approval, no fabricated decisions, and input gating that holds plain prompts in a topic while an interactive prompt is open.
Show subagent activity as cards in the parent session topic, including the child session identity, agent, model, and current tool step, without giving subagents their own topics.

Provide /messages in a session topic to browse user messages and offer revert (roll the session back to a message) and fork (branch a new session from a message that becomes its own topic) through the native session APIs.
Accept file attachments from Telegram into prompts (images, PDF, and text files, bounded in size) and deliver assistant code blocks as files, with album grouping.

Stream assistant output with draft-message streaming and a throttled edit fallback ported from the proven DM-topic delivery patterns: a stable draft id animating an ephemeral preview that the final message dismisses, a durable message mirror map keyed by native message id enabling edit-in-place and exactly-once dedupe, and durable final delivery with boot-drain, plus an adaptive throttle schedule and a message merge window for split mobile input.
Let the owner control visibility of reasoning and tool-call detail and the reply format mode, persisted as runtime settings.
Support restricted corporate networks with a custom Bot API root or an outbound proxy declared in configuration, mutually exclusive, without code changes.

Persist gateway state durably and plugin-scoped through ctx.storage: the Telegram update offset, the bidirectional topic and session map, the message mirror map, pending final deliveries, runtime settings, a schema version, and a bot fingerprint used to reset state when the bot changes, all surviving an OpenCode service restart.

Resync from the native session APIs on startup and after any event-stream break, because the native event stream is live-only and never replays, and reconcile the displayed active topic set to the actual active session set.

Enforce a single-owner allowlist by numeric Telegram user id, keep the bot token out of storage, out of logs, and out of persisted config snapshots, and resolve the token from a ${VAR} placeholder in the process environment using the existing env-substitution contract.

Extend canonical schema v3 with an optional top-level telegram section (enabled, botToken, allowedUserIds, activity window, connectivity, and defaults) and a telegram plugin toggle name, keeping the embedded schema and schemas/vvoc/v3.json in sync and every existing valid config valid.

Contain failures per polling iteration and per update, bound retained state, apply Telegram rate-limit backoff and per-chat send throttling, and provide an enabled kill-switch so a bug or flood storm in the gateway cannot destabilize the host server process.
Keep module contracts, README, package exports, canonical schema, GRACE graph, and GRACE verification synchronized with the implemented behavior.

Constraints.Constraint: The plugin runs inside the pinned OpenCode 2.0.18 server process and uses only the documented Plugin.Context surfaces (session, event, permission, storage, command, model, agent read) plus the existing shared authenticated native runtime for full client operations; it never reads or writes OpenCode's internal SQLite tables.

Exactly one gateway per process: a singleton gate keyed on native app identity prevents a second location's setup from starting a second polling loop, because two bots on one token produce a Telegram 409 conflict and a frozen chat.
Configuration stays strict canonical schema v3; the telegram section is optional so every existing valid config remains valid, and the embedded schema must match schemas/vvoc/v3.json.
Runtime plugins share the startup config snapshot; telegram configuration changes require an OpenCode restart, consistent with every existing runtime plugin.

State is durable and plugin-scoped in ctx.storage; the bot token is never placed in storage, and a changed bot fingerprint resets the stored topic, session, mirror, delivery, settings, and offset maps instead of reusing stale bindings.

The native event stream is live-only with no replay or automatic reconnection, so correctness may not depend on receiving every event; the gateway resyncs from the native session APIs after startup and after any stream end.

One Telegram chat carries one shared message-rate budget across all its topics, so concurrent session topics require per-chat send throttling, coalescing of streamed edits, bounded catch-up, and throttled topic-title edits rather than unbounded immediate delivery.

Stale updates queued while the bot was offline are not executed; messages accepted after an outage window are dropped with a single notice, and the persisted update offset advances only after an update is dispatched.

Permission approvals and question answers are manual and single-owner; no request is auto-approved and no decision is fabricated when a prompt, reply, or permission request disappears outside Telegram.

While an interactive prompt (permission, question, or custom answer) is open in a topic, plain text in that topic is gated rather than sent as a prompt, and the gate is released by completing or cancelling the interaction.

Attachments are bounded in size and count, are downloaded to a temporary location only for admission, and unsupported or oversized attachments are rejected with an explicit notice instead of being silently dropped.
A custom Bot API root and an outbound proxy are mutually exclusive connectivity modes; configuring both is a validation error, and neither is required for normal operation.
The bot supports a single owner in a private chat; group chats, forum supergroups, multi-user access, and the Telegram Business or guest-bot surfaces are out of scope.

Verification must be deterministic: it uses injectable Telegram transport and injectable native runtime boundaries and must not require a real bot token, a live Telegram connection, or live model calls.

Source contracts, README, package exports, canonical schema, GRACE graph, and GRACE verification state remain synchronized with the implemented behavior, and no generated dist output is edited manually.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Do not add a separate process or a vvoc telegram start command; the gateway lives inside the OpenCode server process by explicit user decision.
Do not mirror OpenCode's event-sourced SQLite log, read its internal tables, or model a transcript from database rows.
Do not integrate tmux, herdr, or any multiplexer, and do not key sessions on a terminal window or tab identity.
Do not provide agent switching or agent mode surfaces; sessions use their project default agent by explicit user decision.
Do not expose a compaction trigger; context usage is displayed in /status only, by explicit user decision.
Do not involve the Guardian plugin; permission handling is manual buttons only.
Do not implement pinned topics; the visible topic set tracks active sessions only.

Do not implement git worktree switching, localization, voice or audio transcription, text-to-speech, scheduled tasks, an interactive file browser, MCP browsing, or trusted local shell commands in this change.
Do not add multi-user access, group support, inline mode, mini apps, or bot-to-bot communication.
Do not auto-approve, auto-select, or auto-switch models, agents, or sessions beyond what an explicit owner command requests.
Do not use a live Telegram connection, a real bot token, or live model providers as a repository verification gate.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The TelegramBridgePlugin registers as a native server plugin, is exported from the package root and the ./plugins/telegram subpath, is included in the aggregate server plugin list, and its setup returns a cleanup that aborts the polling loop and releases every acquired runtime.

Setting up the plugin for more than one location in one process starts exactly one gateway; a second setup is a no-op that neither starts a second polling loop nor creates a second General topic, proven by an injected multi-context test.

The gateway long-polls through grammy with a persisted update offset advanced only after dispatch, ignores non-owner senders, ignores messages without a mapped topic, groups message albums from one poll batch, and applies bounded error backoff without ending the loop on a transient failure.

The topology manager creates and maps the fixed General control topic on first use, creates one topic per active session titled from the native session identity, closes (never deletes) a topic when its session leaves the active window (running, or updated within 240 minutes, or created or used through the bot), and reuses the stored topic id when a session becomes active again, proven with an injected Telegram client and clock.

Because the Bot API exposes no list-topics call, the stored topic and session map is authoritative and survives a simulated process restart; a changed bot fingerprint resets the map instead of reusing stale bindings.

/sync is the single idempotent reconciliation command in General: it creates topics for active sessions missing one, closes topics whose sessions left the active set, and reports counts; /new offers a project picker and creates the session with its project default agent; /status reports server health, the active session set with context usage, and the current model per session; /help lists commands.

The topic title carries a leading status emoji reflecting session state, transitions are applied through throttled editForumTopic calls with the clean title preserved after the emoji, and title-edit failures degrade to the last known title without failing the gateway.

/model in a session topic opens an inline picker over connected providers and their models with the current model marked, and a selection is applied through the native session model switch and reflected in /status and the topic lane.

A plain text message in a session topic is admitted as a prompt to that session through the plugin context, streamed output uses draft streaming with a stable draft id and falls back to throttled edits when drafts are unsupported, finals are delivered exactly once through the durable mirror and delivery state, and an abort command interrupts the session.

Permission requests appear as inline-button prompts with once, always, and reject actions, an owner decision is sent through ctx.permission and is never fabricated, a disabled or missing request closes the prompt truthfully, and no request is auto-approved.

Agent questions appear as inline-button prompts with the offered options plus a custom-answer action; choosing custom holds the topic's input gate so the next plain message is the answer rather than a prompt, and completing or cancelling the interaction releases the gate.
Subagent activity is shown as cards in the parent session topic naming the child session, agent, model, and current tool step, and subagents never receive their own topics.

/messages in a session topic lists user messages and offers revert, which rolls the session back to the selected message, and fork, which creates a new session from that message that receives its own active topic.

File attachments (images, PDF, and text files within configured bounds) from a single message or one album are admitted into the prompt, and oversized or unsupported attachments produce an explicit rejection notice.
Reasoning and tool-call visibility and the reply format mode are runtime settings persisted across restarts, with hidden reasoning and compact tool display as defaults.

The telegram section validates enabled, botToken, allowedUserIds, the activity window, connectivity (api root or proxy, mutually exclusive), and defaults; the embedded schema matches schemas/vvoc/v3.json; every previously valid config remains valid; and the telegram plugin toggle disables all registration and starts no gateway.

The bot token is resolved from a ${VAR} placeholder through the existing env-substitution contract, is absent from ctx.storage and from any log or diagnostic, and an unset or empty token disables the gateway with a value-free diagnostic.

Gateway state (offset, topic and session map, message mirror map, pending finals, settings, schema version, bot fingerprint) persists in ctx.storage across a simulated restart, and startup resyncs the active set from the native session APIs so a missed live event cannot leave a permanently stale topic set.

Focused plugin, topology, delivery, config, and schema tests pass together with the repository check, build, pack, and GRACE gates; a live Telegram session is documented as a manual step and is not a repository gate.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh deterministic output proves: one gateway per process under multi-context setup; offset persistence and post-dispatch advancement with an injected transport; topic create, close, reuse, restart-survival, and status-emoji title transitions with an injected Telegram client and clock; General commands including the project picker, /sync reconciliation, /status with context usage, and /model selection; prompt streaming with draft and edit fallback, exactly-once finals through the mirror and delivery state, and abort; manual permission and question flows including the custom-answer input gate; subagent cards; /messages revert and fork; bounded attachments; runtime settings persistence; schema acceptance and rejection with the embedded schema equal to schemas/vvoc/v3.json including mutual exclusivity of connectivity modes; token placeholder resolution, storage exclusion, and value-free diagnostics; per-iteration failure containment and rate-limit backoff. No real bot token, live Telegram connection, or live model call is used, and the live-connection walkthrough is documented as a manual step.

Assumptions.Assumption: The user explicitly chose the in-process server plugin form over a separate process, grammy as the Telegram client library, a 240-minute active-session window with close-not-delete, a single /sync command, status emoji in topic titles, model switching without agent switching, manual permission buttons without Guardian, no compaction trigger, file attachments inbound, message revert and fork, subagent cards, no worktree or localization, and proxy or custom API root support for corporate networks; the only decision pending at draft time is overall spec approval.

ctx.storage is documented as durable and plugin-scoped, so gateway state survives an OpenCode service restart; if the durability guarantee or plugin scoping proves false during implementation, the fallback is a file store under $XDG_DATA_HOME/vvoc/telegram/, which is a planning decision rather than a scope change.

Draft-message streaming (sendMessageDraft and sendRichMessageDraft with a stable draft id, with the final send dismissing the draft) and the mirror, outbox, and throttled-edit patterns proven in the vv-chat Telegram service are portable to this plugin's delivery layer; where the Bot API reports a method unsupported, delivery degrades to throttled edits.

Private-chat forum topics are supported for the bot through BotFather and the Bot API exposes them through message_thread_id on sends and createForumTopic in a private chat; if the field shape differs at implementation time the adapter isolates it and no spec requirement changes.

The native plugin context exposes session create, get, prompt, interrupt, update, command, compact, wait, model and agent reads, and permission list, get, and reply; full session listing, active-session reads, revert, and fork use the existing shared authenticated native runtime client rather than the narrower context session surface.
New sessions are created with their project's default agent, which the user's vvoc setup sets to vv-controller, so no agent selection surface is required.
The bot runs as a single owner in a private chat and the owner's numeric Telegram user id is supplied in configuration; this is the entire access-control boundary for this change.
